title: Define compact direct-prompt retention with the actual delivery owner before enabling production journal writes
outcome: Stage B supplies compact retained identity and a safe body/evidence retirement seam owned by actual primary PromptDelivery, so a busy session is bounded by live retained work rather than a lifetime prompt count. Production journal writes remain explicitly unavailable until this contract and adapter are validated.
acceptance: Production journal writes remain blocked until the real primary delivery owner proves when body and large evidence are no longer needed; timeout, queue acknowledgement and uncertainty alone never authorize compaction.

Compact retention preserves original source creation/key, operation identity, intent digest and required historical facts so exact retries cannot recreate execution and conflicting reuse remains refused.
Live body/evidence bytes are bounded independently of legacy mailbox/wake quotas, without a permanent lifetime prompt-count cutoff, TTL identity eviction or a separate lifecycle owner.
Meaningful behavioral tests cover settled compaction, unresolved outcomes, conflicting retries, restart and authority cuts through the actual owner before mounting.
